# Lott's conjecture on lower bounds for Hodge-Laplacian eigenvalues

Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$n∈N, $\kappa\in\mathbb{R}$κ∈R, and $\nu,D>0$ν,D>0. For a connected oriented closed Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$(M n,g), let $\mu^{(p)}_1$μ 1(p)​ denote the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Hodge-Laplacian on $p$p-forms. Assume

$$\operatorname{sec}_g\geq\kappa,\qquad \operatorname{diam}(M)\leq D,\qquad \operatorname{Vol}(g)\geq\nu.$$sec g​≥κ,diam(M)≤D,Vol(g)≥ν.

Lott's conjecture. There exists a positive constant $C(n,\kappa,\nu,D)>0$C(n,κ,ν,D)>0, depending only on $n$n, $\kappa$κ, $\nu$ν, and $D$D, such that

$$\mu^{(p)}_1\geq C(n,\kappa,\nu,D),\qquad \text{for all }p=0,1,\ldots,n.$$μ 1(p)​≥C(n,κ,ν,D),for all p=0,1,…,n.

This conjecture asks whether a lower sectional-curvature bound, together with diameter and volume bounds, suffices to give uniform positive lower bounds for the first nonzero Hodge-Laplacian eigenvalues. It is an alternative to the known result under a two-sided sectional-curvature bound, and remains open as far as the authors know.

Title: Eigenvalue Estimates of the Hodge Laplacian Under Lower Ricci Curvature Bound
Authors: Anusha Bhattacharya, Soma Maity, Aditya Tiwari
Date: Thu Feb 12 13:08:53 2026

We establish uniform lower and upper bounds for the eigenvalues of the Hodge Laplacian acting on differential forms on closed Riemannian manifolds with a lower Ricci curvature bound, a positive lower bound on the injectivity radius, and an upper bound on the diameter. Our results extend earlier work of Dodziuk, Lott, and Mantuano, which required bounded sectional curvature, to the broader setting of lower Ricci curvature bounds. As applications, we obtain uniform eigenvalue bounds for the connection Laplacian acting on $1$-forms and establish a global Poincaré inequality for differential forms under the same geometric assumptions.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Abstract

We establish geometric lower bounds for the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Hodge Laplacian in the class of non-convex domains given by Euclidean annular regions with a convex outer boundary and a spherical inner boundary. A more refined version of these bounds were obtained by Savo [26], also for convex Euclidean domains:

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{C_2}{D_p(\mathcal {D})^2}\le \mu ^{(p)}_1(\mathcal {D})\le \frac{C_3}{D_p(\mathcal {D})^2},\qquad \forall \, p \in \{1,\dots ,n\}, \end{aligned}$$

where \(C_2\) and \(C_3\) are explicit constants depending only on n and p; \(D_p(\mathcal {D})\) is the length of the \(p^\text {th}\) longest principal axis of the largest ellipsoid that can be inscribed in \(\mathcal {D}\), known as the John ellipsoid. For example, \(D_1(\mathcal {D})\) corresponds to the diameter, and \(D_n(\mathcal {D})\) corresponds to the inradius of \(\mathcal {D}\). These bounds were also generalised for sufficiently small geodesically convex domains in manifolds with non-negative curvature operator [19].

Furthermore, for \(p\in \{0,\dots ,n-2\}\), Guerini [16, Theorem 2.1] constructed non-convex domains diffeomorphic to balls, with bounded diameters, which have an arbitrarily small positive eigenvalue for p-forms. The convexity assumption in [17] is a means to avoid the creation of non-trivial cohomology through collapsing as done in [16] by gluing a thick and a thin part that generalise the classical Cheeger dumbbell.

The lower bounds of this article for Euclidean annular regions depend on the distance between the inner hole and the outer boundary, which we refer to as the contact radius \(R_c\) (Figure 1).

We now state the main results.

### Theorem 1.1

Let \(\mathfrak {D}\subset \mathbb {R}^n\) be a Euclidean annular domain, given by a smooth, bounded convex domain minus a hole. Then the following lower bounds hold for the smallest exact eigenvalue of the Hodge Laplacian on p-forms.

  1. (1)

For \(n\ge 3\) and \(p\in \{2,\dots ,n-1\}\),

$$\begin{aligned} \mu ^{{(p)}}_{{1,{{\,\mathrm{{\text {ex}}}\,}}}}(\mathfrak {D})\ge K \frac{1}{D^2}\left( \frac{R_c}{D} \right) ^{5n^2-n-5}. \end{aligned}$$

  2. (2)

For \(n\ge 2\) and \(p=1\),

$$\begin{aligned} \mu ^{{(1)}}_{{1,{{\,\mathrm{{\text {ex}}}\,}}}}(\mathfrak {D})\ge K \frac{1}{D^2}\left( \frac{R_c}{D}\right) ^{11n-5}. \end{aligned}$$

Here, D and \(R_c\) denote the diameter and the contact radius of \(\mathfrak {D}\), respectively.

## Abstract

Let M be an m-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. We obtain the upper bounds of the harmonic mean of the first m nonzero Neumann eigenvalues and Steklov eigenvalues involving the conformal volume and relative conformal volume, respectively. We also give an optimal sharp extrinsic upper bound for closed submanifolds in space forms. These extend the previous related results for the first nonzero eigenvalues.
